bounds: Kani checks the actual count/byte admission predicate over all usize inputs. Allocation, JSON parsing, async I/O and operating-system progress remain outside this numeric proof.

The finite duplex projection has one-slot pipes, two outbound chunks, two or three inbound chunks, a two-frame queue, cancellation and overflow. Weakly fair I/O reaches an explicit terminal outcome. Rust async wiring and actual adapter behavior require the linked regressions; no automatic implementation refinement is claimed.

Two retry keys and fingerprints, atomic Session root CAS; acceptance and final close are absorbing alternatives. SQLite and HTTP tests exercise implementation boundaries but no universal Rust/SQL or transport refinement is claimed.

The Worker lifecycle now consumes one private production decision over the full u128 proof-age and proof-window domains and every due, proven, lost and unknown observation class. Kani proves that an at-or-beyond-window observation always closes and that refresh is possible only for a proven observation still inside the prior window. Both initial pool admission and the recurring provider monitor use this same boundary; a successful recurring probe anchors the next proof at request start.

WorkerAuthorityEvidence additionally checks two finite independent proof ages 0 through 4, request latency retained in evidence age, one single-flight probe, absorbing closure and eventual closure when either environment evidence or Registry renewal stops under its stated fairness. Paused-time unit tests cover before, exact and after-deadline response schedules; Worker lifecycle tests cover startup rejection, drift, stalls, transient recovery and continuing Registry heartbeats. The production-kernel proof does not establish Tokio scheduling, Instant or operating-system clock correctness, provider policy truth, Registry transport behavior, physical cleanup or universal async refinement.

One admitted execution and one Linux namespace compose the existing GO/close model with live/stopping/exited init observations. Renewal additionally bounds absolute cutoffs to 1..3, clock to 0..4, one queued frame and a stalled proper prefix. Clock and kernel progress require explicit weak fairness. Business lease renewal, Session-wide production wiring, kernel correctness, hostile-host escape and real elapsed-time bounds are not proved. Ordinary LocalProcess crash semantics remain unchanged.

Recovery composes the same single-execution boundary with one durable Ready/Removing/Removed marker lock, two competing recovery entrances, and known/unknown OS observation. It checks pre-GO persistence, crash retention and quiescence before resource/deletion effects. Exact filesystem CAS, procfs identity truth, multi-execution refinement, reboot liveness and current Session adapter installation are outside this abstract proof. Linux provider tests exercise two participants and actual owner SIGKILL. Session stop composition adds independent Hand quiescence and a receipt requiring both Hand and execution evidence; unknown Hand cannot justify resource effects or a Session receipt. Runtime-host Linux tests exercise stop, quiesce and disposal with two scopes and injected uncertain Hand/observer receipts.

Kani checks the actual lease_epoch transition over the full i64 x bool input domain, using shared StoredU64 checked arithmetic and an independent i128 specification. This is a numeric transition proof, not SQL locking, bearer entropy, queue linearizability, or universal implementation refinement.

The negative TLC control restores the resident bypass. This is a model link plus executed integration tests, not a full asynchronous Rust refinement or a guarantee against failure after observation.
